ops.title: Concept extraction: the connectivity premise is refuted, and regex beats the encoder 10,000x
ops.body:
Measured 2026-07-26 over **775 records from 11 repos** carrying `refs/cc-notes/*` (monorepo: 94). Scripts and hand-checks under `/tmp/ccn-exec/P6spec/` (machine-local; the numbers below are the durable part). No repo was edited.

The plan asserted that "because there are no note→note edges and most monorepo notes are untagged, concept extraction is **the only thing that creates entity↔entity connectivity at all**." That is wrong in three separate ways.

**1. The graph is already connected.** Monorepo baseline from tags + anchors + branch + session + declared task edges: **4 components, 94% of entities in the largest, 1 isolate, median degree 20**. All-repos: 99 components, 9% isolated, median degree 12. Even the harshest honest variant (session edges removed, hub terms capped): 24 components, 62% largest, 20% isolated — that is *sparse*, not disconnected. Adding any extractor drives monorepo to 1 component / median degree 26 of 93, i.e. saturation. **Component count was the wrong objective.**

**2. "Most monorepo notes carry no tags" is false, and it named the wrong kind.** 44% of monorepo *notes* are untagged; only 8% carry neither tag nor anchor; monorepo *docs* are 0% untagged. The untagged kind is **tasks — 59% globally**. And tasks carry **zero anchors, 290 of 290**, so anchors contribute **0 note↔task edges corpus-wide**. The disconnection is real but it is entirely a task-layer problem, not a tagging problem.

**3. The three clusters named as proof are among the best-tagged material in the corpus.** `sandsql` is the 3rd most common tag (21 uses), `repo-shrink` 6th (14). Live `cc-notes search` already finds them: sandsql 20 hits, pulumi 11, repo-shrink 6 — covering 10/10 of pulumi's searchable-kind members and 5/6 of repo-shrink's.

**What concepts actually buy is discrimination, not connectivity.** Same-topic pair recall over 703 labelled monorepo pairs: baseline P.83/R.43/**F1 .57** → +regex .79/.59/**F1 .68** → +GLiNER .79/.55/**F1 .65**.

**The encoder loses outright.** GLiNER `urchade/gliner_multi-v2.1` (289M, CPU, M5 Max): **2001 s** total, median 1815 ms/doc, p90 4601 ms/doc. Identifier regex: **0.2 s**, 0.2 ms/doc — ~10,000×. Hand-checked n=30 each: across all spans GLiNER wins on precision 67% vs 47%, but **on edge-bearing spans (df≥2) GLiNER collapses to 37% against regex's 67%** — 72% of GLiNER's terms are singletons that create no edge, and what survives is dominated by bare version numbers (`0.16.0`, `v0.21.3`, `2026-07-13`). Its zero-shot label taxonomy failed: 67% of spans landed on `library`, and `subsystem` fired 53 times across 775 documents. Two rescue configs (threshold 0.3 → F1 .66; re-worded labels → F1 .57, zero gain) did not close the gap.

Orphan attachment on the no-session baseline, over sandsql's 22 untagged members: baseline 1/22 → GLiNER 16/22 → **regex 21/22** (purity .43→.53). Pulumi 0/6 → 5/6 → 6/6, but purity only .16–.30 — attachment is not clustering, and the purity numbers say so.

**The free signal nobody is using: the per-op `session` id.** Available today in `history --json`. Standalone it scores **F1 .48** — above tags (.38), above the raw regex (.45), and near the entire GLiNER run (.51). It costs nothing to compute.

## Consequences

- **Drop the GLiNER/encoder lane from Phase 6.** Ship the identifier regex with a document-frequency cap (42% of its edge mass is each repo's own name — `cc-notes` df=167, `capt-hook` df=168) and a bare-version filter.
- **Wire the session edge first.** Best return per line of code in the whole design.
- **The task layer is the real disconnection**, which promotes two Phase-T items from housekeeping to load-bearing: tasks must reach code (they have no anchors at all), and tasks must enter the search corpus.
- **Stop optimizing component count.** The Phase 5 objective is discrimination — same-topic pair F1 and the superseded-leak rate — not reachability.
